title: Oil Tops $104 as US-Iran Peace Talks Hit a Wall
excerpt: Trump calls Iran's ceasefire counteroffer 'garbage,' renewing fears of a prolonged Hormuz shutdown and a global energy crisis
body:
Brent crude futures surged nearly 3% to settle at $104.21 a barrel on Monday after President Donald Trump declared the US-Iran ceasefire was on 'massive life support' — and dismissed Tehran's latest peace counteroffer in the bluntest possible terms.

**What happened:**
Trump rejected Iran's response to a US ceasefire proposal, calling it 'totally unacceptable' and warning that negotiations were at near-collapse. Iran had proposed a staggered approach — ending the war first, with nuclear talks deferred to a later stage. Trump, by contrast, has demanded Iran formally halt its nuclear program and hand over an estimated 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium before any sanctions relief. The gap between the two sides remains stark, and no new talks have been confirmed.

**Why this matters:**
The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively shut for ten straight weeks — the largest oil supply disruption in history, according to market analysts. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned this week that the market is losing roughly 100 million barrels of supply each week, and that 'if reopening is delayed by a few more weeks, normalization will last into 2027.' Citi analysts noted that risks to oil prices remain tilted to the upside, as Iran retains significant control over the timing of any reopening. Goldman Sachs separately flagged that easily accessible buffers of refined products — naphtha, LPG, and jet fuel — are being depleted rapidly, raising the specter of localized shortages.

**What to watch next:**
All eyes now fall on whether Pakistan and Qatar, the two key mediators, can coax both sides back to the table before the ceasefire fully unravels — and before oil markets price in an even worse scenario.
